subject: Agriculture
title: What Is Agroecology?
description: A quick win: understand What Is Agroecology?.

hook.text: Agroecology treats farms as ecosystems, not factories. The science is ecology; the subject is agriculture.

buildup.text: Instead of fighting nature with chemicals, agroecology designs farms that work with ecological processes.

discovery.text: Diverse plantings attract predators that control pests. Healthy soil microbiomes feed plants. Water cycles are restored.

twist.text: Agroecology challenges corporate agriculture. There are no expensive inputs to sell—knowledge replaces products.

climax.text: The UN's Food and Agriculture Organization endorsed agroecology in 2018 as key to sustainable food systems.

punchline.text: Farm like an ecosystem. Ecology is the textbook; the field is the classroom.

quiz.question: How does agroecology fundamentally differ from industrial agriculture?
options: It treats farms as ecosystems and uses ecological processes instead of chemical inputs

details.summary: Agroecology applies ecological principles to the design and management of farming systems. It treats farms as ecosystems, emphasizing biodiversity, nutrient cycling, and natural pest control rather than external chemical inputs.
details.whyItMatters: Agroecology offers a science-based framework for redesigning food systems to be more resilient, equitable, and environmentally sound. The United Nations has endorsed it as a key pathway to sustainable food security.
takeaways: Agroecology designs farms as ecosystems using biodiversity and natural processes
It integrates ecological science with traditional farming knowledge systems
The UN recognizes agroecology as essential for achieving sustainable food security

faq.question: How is agroecology different from conventional organic farming?
faq.answer: Agroecology goes beyond input substitution (replacing synthetic chemicals with organic ones) to redesign the entire farming system. It integrates crops, livestock, trees, and beneficial insects into a functioning ecosystem that provides its own fertility and pest management.

faq.question: Why has the United Nations endorsed agroecology?
faq.answer: UN reports found agroecology can double food production in vulnerable regions while reducing environmental damage, improving farmer livelihoods, and building climate resilience. It addresses hunger, biodiversity loss, and climate change simultaneously.
